editorial:
Imagine being a teenager in the 80s where the government controls everything you say and hear. That is exactly where you find Mihkel, a loud and proud musician who just wants to rock out in Soviet-era Estonia. He spends most of his time fighting with his rival, Hendrik, but they both have one goal: getting noticed by a Finnish talent scout. You get to follow this mismatched group of kids as they pile into a car and head across the country to a massive rock festival. Along the way, Mihkel tries to win over Liisa, and the whole trip feels like one big, messy adventure filled with loud music and teenage angst.

The chemistry between the leads is great, and the movie does a wonderful job showing how music can make you feel free even when you are trapped. While the middle part drags a bit, the energy picks up once they hit the festival. If you enjoy stories about friendship and chasing dreams, you will love this. It is a great pick for anyone who misses the vibe of old school coming-of-age films.
endingExplained: At the big festival, Mihkel and Hendrik stop fighting and actually play together, showing the scout their combined talent. While the scout is impressed, the movie ends with a bittersweet twist: they realize that the music was more important than the fame. They do not all leave for Finland, but they find peace with themselves. The final scene shows them back home, feeling braver and more connected to their culture than ever before.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music and stories about growing up.
